newsitem.title: SWEDEN: US urges Estonia, Latvia to help ethnic Russians.
newsitem.headline: US urges Estonia, Latvia to help ethnic Russians.

text.p: A senior U.S. diplomat strongly advised Estonia and Latvia on Tuesday to do more for their ethnic Russians to help pave the way for joining NATO.

U.S. ambassador to Sweden Thomas Siebert said the two Baltic former Soviet republics, who declared independence in 1991, needed to do a lot more for the Russian communities still living within their borders.
"There are sizeable ethnic Russian communities living in Estonia and Latvia and their welfare remains a concern," Siebert said in a speech to a Swedish business seminar.
"Estonia and Latvia have taken laudable concrete steps to integrate these communities, but more work needs to be done and we are working with them."
Most Russians remaining in Latvia and Estonia since independence do not have citizenship and some say they have been deliberately shut out of political life.
Siebert said action to integrate the Russian communities was one of the issues Estonia and Latvia needed to address as they bid to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
"They need to further consolidate their democratic institutions and military establishments," he said.

Both countries and and neighbouring Lithuania are seeking to join the 16-member security alliance as it expands eastwards to ensure themselves a place in the new European security system out of the shadow of Russia.

Diplomatic sources behind closed doors have already dismissed the Baltic states' chances of being admitted in the first round of expansion of NATO, expecting likely entrants to be Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
Siebert said that for the United States "the question of NATO membership for the Baltic States is not if but when".
"We are firmly committed to helping them prepare for NATO membership and take this commitment very seriously."
